title: Twenty First Word First Station Third Warning Impatience And Three Kinds Of Patience

questions.question: In this part, who is being spoken to?
questions.answer: The person’s own self, or nafs.

questions.question: What problem does the nafs have at the start of this part?
questions.answer: It is acting impatient.

questions.question: What two time periods does the nafs wrongly worry about?
questions.answer: The past and the future.

questions.question: What kinds of old things from the past make the nafs upset?
questions.answer: Earlier hard times in worship, prayer, and troubles.

questions.question: What kinds of things from the future does the nafs imagine and then get upset about?
questions.answer: Future acts of worship, prayer duties, and disasters.

questions.question: What example is given about a leader who makes bad choices?
questions.answer: A commander moves soldiers to places that do not need help and leaves the middle weak.

questions.question: What happens because the center is left weak?
questions.answer: The enemy attacks there and wins.

questions.question: What lesson does that army example teach?
questions.answer: A person should not waste strength by worrying the wrong way.

questions.question: What has happened to the pain from yesterday?
questions.answer: It is gone now.

questions.question: What good thing stays after yesterday’s hardship is over?
questions.answer: Its reward and good results remain.

questions.question: Why is it foolish to feel tired now because of future days?
questions.answer: Those days have not come yet.

questions.question: What everyday example shows how silly that worry is?
questions.answer: It is like crying today about being hungry or thirsty later.

questions.question: How should a person think about worship today?
questions.answer: As a good and noble act that takes a little effort and brings big reward.

questions.question: What can bitter sadness turn into when a person thinks rightly?
questions.answer: Sweet effort and fresh energy.

questions.question: What three kinds of patience are named?
questions.answer: Patience in worship, patience in staying away from sin, and patience during disasters.

questions.question: If a person uses patience in the right way, what can it help with?
questions.answer: It can help the person stand firm through hardships and troubles.

questions.question: What is the name of this section in the target passage?
questions.answer: The Third Warning.

questions.question: What bad habit is being corrected in this warning?
questions.answer: Being impatient.

questions.question: What does the warning say about thinking too much about old hardships?
questions.answer: It makes a person upset for no good reason.

questions.question: What does the warning say about thinking too much about future duties and troubles?
questions.answer: It makes a person bored and tired before those things even come.

questions.question: In the comparison, what kind of person is described?
questions.answer: A foolish military leader.

questions.question: What mistake does that leader make with the soldiers on the right side?
questions.answer: He sends more soldiers there even though that side already has help.

questions.question: What mistake does he make with the soldiers on the left side?
questions.answer: He sends many there even though there is no enemy there.

questions.question: What important place is left without enough soldiers?
questions.answer: The center.

questions.question: What happens after the enemy notices the center is weak?
questions.answer: They attack it and defeat him.

questions.question: In this warning, what are yesterday’s hardships changed into?
questions.answer: Mercy, blessings, and reward.

questions.question: After a hard time passes, which remains: the pain or the good result?
questions.answer: The good result remains.

questions.question: What should a person do instead of becoming weary?
questions.answer: Keep going with fresh eagerness.

questions.question: Why is worrying now about future worship called unreasonable?
questions.answer: Because the future is not here yet.

questions.question: What should a reasonable person focus on in worship?
questions.answer: Today only.

questions.question: About how much time does the passage say to spend from the day on this service?
questions.answer: One hour.

questions.question: What special words are given to say while carrying patience?
questions.answer: Calling on the Most Patient One.

questions.question: Which part of a person is warned in this passage?
questions.answer: The impatient self.

questions.question: What is not sensible to do with past hardships?
questions.answer: To keep thinking about them and feeling upset now.

questions.question: What is not sensible to do with future troubles?
questions.answer: To imagine them now and lose patience.

questions.question: What story is used to explain this mistake?
questions.answer: A story about a commander using his army badly.

questions.question: Did the commander strengthen the middle or weaken it?
questions.answer: He weakened it.

questions.question: Why was sending soldiers to the left side a bad idea?
questions.answer: There were no enemy soldiers there.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about yesterday’s pain?
questions.answer: It has passed away.

questions.question: What can hardship become after it is over?
questions.answer: A blessing and a reward.

questions.question: What kind of effort should replace weariness?
questions.answer: Serious effort with new excitement.

questions.question: What makes worrying about future days a kind of foolishness?
questions.answer: A person is suffering before those days even arrive.

questions.question: What simple example helps explain that foolishness?
questions.answer: Acting hungry or thirsty today because of later need.

questions.question: How is the act of worship described when a person thinks correctly?
questions.answer: Pleasant, uplifting, and worth a lot.

questions.question: What can happen to a person’s gloomy feelings?
questions.answer: They can change into cheerful striving.

questions.question: How many kinds of patience are listed?
questions.answer: Three.

questions.question: What are those three kinds of patience about?
questions.answer: Worship, avoiding sin, and facing disaster.

questions.question: Who gave the person the strength to be patient?
questions.answer: Almighty Allah.

questions.question: What should a person do with that patience-strength?
questions.answer: Use it properly and hold firm.

questions.question: What main character trait is being taught in this passage?
questions.answer: Patience.

questions.question: What does the speaker ask the nafs about old prayer hardships and troubles?
questions.answer: Why it keeps bringing them to mind and becoming distressed.

questions.question: What does the speaker ask the nafs about future worship and disasters?
questions.answer: Why it imagines them now and acts impatient.

questions.question: What kind of commander is used in the comparison?
questions.answer: A foolish one.

questions.question: In the comparison, what unusual thing happened on the right side?
questions.answer: It had become a place of support, not danger.

questions.question: Even though the left side had no enemy, what did the commander do there?
questions.answer: He sent many soldiers there.

questions.question: What was the result of these bad choices?
questions.answer: The center had no protection.

questions.question: What happened next in the battle story?
questions.answer: The enemy attacked the center and defeated him.

questions.question: How should a person view yesterday’s worship hardships now?
questions.answer: As something finished that left good reward behind.

questions.question: What should not happen after remembering that pain is gone?
questions.answer: A person should not become tired of worship.

questions.question: Why should future days not make a person weary today?
questions.answer: Because they are still not here.

questions.question: What example from daily life is used about future need?
questions.answer: Crying now over food or drink that will be needed later.

questions.question: What sentence idea should a reasonable person say to himself about today?
questions.answer: I can give one hour today for a beautiful act of service with great reward.

questions.question: What can sweeten a person’s attitude toward worship?
questions.answer: Thinking about its goodness and reward.

questions.question: What is the first type of patience named?
questions.answer: Patience in worship.

questions.question: What is the second type of patience named?
questions.answer: Patience in leaving sins.

questions.question: What is the third type of patience named?
questions.answer: Patience during disasters.

questions.question: What should a person do with the patience Allah gave?
questions.answer: Keep using it rightly to endure troubles.

questions.question: What is the title of the passage section between the markers?
questions.answer: Third Warning.

questions.question: Who is told, “You are charged with being patient”?
questions.answer: The nafs, or self.

questions.question: What wrong way of thinking makes the self suffer about the past?
questions.answer: Remembering old hard times and getting upset again.

questions.question: What wrong way of thinking makes the self suffer about the future?
questions.answer: Imagining future duties and troubles before they happen.

questions.question: What picture is used to show this mistake clearly?
questions.answer: A battle scene with a commander and soldiers.

questions.question: What foolish choice does the commander make after help comes on one side?
questions.answer: He keeps sending more soldiers there.

questions.question: What foolish choice does he make on the side with no enemy at all?
questions.answer: He sends many soldiers there too.

questions.question: What key place loses all its soldiers because of that?
questions.answer: The center.

questions.question: What final result comes from leaving the center empty?
questions.answer: The enemy defeats him.

questions.question: What happened to the hard feelings from yesterday?
questions.answer: They passed away.

questions.question: What remains from yesterday’s hard worship or trouble?
questions.answer: The joy, blessing, and reward.

questions.question: What should a person do instead of feeling worn out by the past?
questions.answer: Continue with strong effort.

questions.question: What makes present worry about future days so unreasonable?
questions.answer: Those days do not exist yet for us.

questions.question: Which two body needs are used as examples of future worry?
questions.answer: Hunger and thirst.

questions.question: How much of the day is described as being spent in worship?
questions.answer: One hour.

questions.question: How is the service of worship described in this warning?
questions.answer: Good, pleasing, elevated, and lightly difficult.

questions.question: What can happen when bitter discouragement is replaced the right way?
questions.answer: It becomes sweet striving.

questions.question: What should patience be used for in all three areas named?
questions.answer: To stay steady in worship, avoid sin, and bear disasters.

questions.question: What kind of self is being corrected in this target passage?
questions.answer: An impatient self.

questions.question: What does the passage say about feeling upset over old worship struggles today?
questions.answer: It is not wise.

questions.question: What does the passage say about feeling upset now over future prayer duties?
questions.answer: It is also not wise.

questions.question: What large comparison helps explain this lesson?
questions.answer: A commander making poor choices in war.

questions.question: What happened to the commander’s right side in the comparison?
questions.answer: It had become supported by joined forces.

questions.question: Why was it senseless to send soldiers to the left side?
questions.answer: No enemy was there.

questions.question: Which part was left too weak because of all this moving around?
questions.answer: The middle.

questions.question: How did the enemy use that mistake?
questions.answer: It attacked the weak middle.

questions.question: When the passage looks back at yesterday’s pain, what does it say about it now?
questions.answer: It is gone.

questions.question: What good things can remain after difficulty is over?
questions.answer: Mercy, blessing, pleasure, and reward.

questions.question: What attitude should replace feeling weary?
questions.answer: New eagerness and enthusiasm.

questions.question: Why is worrying about future worship compared to acting hungry before hunger comes?
questions.answer: Because both are suffering too early.

questions.question: What should a reasonable person say about today’s worship time?
questions.answer: That spending one hour on it is worth it.

questions.question: How is the reward of that act described?
questions.answer: Great.

questions.question: How is its hardship described?
questions.answer: Small.

questions.question: What are the three patience jobs a person must carry?
questions.answer: Worship, staying away from sin, and enduring disasters.

questions.question: What should a person not do with the patience Allah gave?
questions.answer: Waste it in the wrong way.

questions.question: If patience is used well, what will it be enough for?
questions.answer: For standing against every hardship and disaster.
